goals: Mechanistic: quantify how water partitioning (ET, surface runoff, sub-surface drainage, snow storage/melt) shifts between a wet year (1993) and a dry year (2002), and how that shift varies along the basin's elevation/climate gradient
Validation: check simulated water balance against available in-domain observations (USGS gauges), honestly scoped given no routing
key_processes: precipitation partitioning into ET vs runoff vs drainage
snow accumulation/melt at high elevation and its seasonal timing
soil-moisture storage change between wet and dry years

model_choice.rationale: Single-column ELM directly simulates the ET/runoff/drainage/snow partitioning targeted; the wet/dry contrast is a forcing-period treatment, the framework's native strength, and Arizona is inside CONUS so year- and location-specific NLDAS forcing is available.

answerable: Wet-year vs dry-year contrast in ET / surface runoff / sub-surface drainage / snow at each column (year-specific NLDAS forcing)
Coarse variation of that contrast across elevation bands (NLDAS resolves ~12 km precip/temperature gradients, including orographic signal)
Change in soil-moisture and snow storage between the two years

not_answerable.aspect: Validation of partitioning against USGS stream gauge discharge
not_answerable.why: Single-column ELM has no lateral routing; column runoff/drainage cannot be integrated into channel streamflow for gauge comparison

not_answerable.aspect: Fine elevation control on snow and precipitation within 12 km cells
not_answerable.why: NLDAS is 0.125 deg with no sub-cell lapse-rate downscaling; ridgetop SWE will be underestimated over ~2400 m of relief

sampling_strategy.approach: stratified (elevation/climate band x dominant soil), forcing-period contrast applied within each column
sampling_strategy.n_justification: The question is a 2-level forcing contrast (wet/dry), which each column carries internally; N is set by the need to span the elevation/climate gradient (3 bands) crossed with the two dominant soil textures, plus one extra valley/riparian column where partitioning between runoff and drainage is most sensitive. Seven columns span the strata without a blind dense grid.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: One-to-two columns per elevation band spanning the ~900-3300 m relief; oversample the valley/riparian corridor (runoff vs recharge partitioning most sensitive there) and place a high-band column in the snow-influenced White Mountain headwaters to capture the largest wet/dry snow signal (noting ridgetop SWE will be low-biased).
sampling_strategy.replication: Light: two soil variants per band where texture contrast plausibly reorders runoff vs drainage; no pure replication.

sampling_plan.group: valley / semi-arid low elevation (900-1500 m), coarse soil
sampling_plan.reason: Captures the driest, most ET-and-infiltration-dominated end where the wet/dry runoff response is flashiest; coarse soil favors drainage over surface runoff.

sampling_plan.group: mid-elevation transition (1500-2300 m), coarse + finer soil
sampling_plan.reason: Samples the rain/mixed zone where soil texture most strongly reorders runoff vs sub-surface drainage between wet and dry years.

sampling_plan.group: high / snow-influenced headwaters (2300-3300 m), upland soil
sampling_plan.reason: Captures the snow-accumulation-and-melt regime that should show the largest wet-year vs dry-year storage and melt-timing difference (SWE low-biased by 12 km forcing).
Oversampled point where partitioning between surface runoff and recharge is most sensitive and most relevant to downstream flow.

validation_design.comparison: aggregated — area-weighted sum of column runoff+drainage compared to gauge discharge as a coarse water-balance sanity check; NOT co-located and NOT routed, so timing/attenuation cannot be assessed
validation_design.metric: annual/seasonal volume bias between wet and dry years
validation_design.n_validation_points: unknown — depends on gauge count within HUC 15060103

validation_design.comparison: analog — SNOTEL is sparse/missing in-domain; only a qualitative analog check against regional SNOTEL is possible, expecting low bias at ridgetops
validation_design.metric: qualitative direction/magnitude of wet-vs-dry peak SWE

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: wet year (1993) vs dry year (2002) NLDAS forcing per column, native SSURGO soil, WTD-informed warm start plus short spin-up

requires_capabilities.why: convert independent column runoff+drainage into comparable streamflow
requires_capabilities.blocks: quantitative validation against USGS gauge discharge

requires_capabilities.why: NLDAS 0.125 deg cannot resolve within-cell terrain over ~2400 m relief
requires_capabilities.blocks: accurate high-elevation snow/precip and fine elevation control

requires_capabilities.why: ensure wet/dry contrast reflects meteorology not cold-start artifacts
requires_capabilities.blocks: credible interannual storage and drainage comparison

requires_capabilities.why: assign per-column soil texture across bands

requires_capabilities.capability: DEM / elevation sampling and HUC boundary resolver
requires_capabilities.why: place columns in correct elevation bands within HUC 15060103

assumptions: 1993 is representatively wet and 2002 representatively dry for this basin within the 1980-2018 NLDAS record
Higher elevations lie generally toward the White Mountains (northeast) of the bbox; concrete coordinates require DEM sampling
USGS gauge(s) exist within the HUC; count and location to be resolved from the gauge inventory
open_questions: Which specific USGS gauge(s) fall inside HUC 15060103, and do their drainage areas match the sampled columns?
Should additional years be added to establish a wet/dry percentile baseline, or is the 1993/2002 pair fixed by the user?
Is a basin-aggregated (unrouted) runoff comparison acceptable, or is routed streamflow required (would trigger the routing backlog item)?
